3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: Sordland One's flight from Holsord to Wraclawitz took approximately five hours. Despite heavy turbulence, I managed to sleep a little.

4.speaker: Narrator
4.text: Symon, Deivid and I landed at the international airport of the capital city of Wehlen. Our aim here was to finalise the trade deal drafted between Sordland and Wehlen.

5.speaker: Narrator
5.text: Our plane landed, and the door opened. The sun blinded me for a moment. I stepped outside.

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: I saw the soldiers lined up on either side of a red carpet. There must've been at least a hundred of them. A marching band started playing and the soldiers immediately saluted me.

9.speaker: Player_Italic
9.text: Proceed to the red carpet without any gestures.

10.speaker: Narrator
10.text: At the bottom of the stairs, Wiktor Smolak was waiting for me next to a military jeep with a few soldiers by his side. There were a few reporters at the edge of the crowd, waiting with their cameras.

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: He was a tall man, almost as tall as me. He was wearing large sunglasses and a regular suit, contrasting with the military attire of everyone else in the field.

13.speaker: Narrator
13.text: He immediately motioned for an embrace. We hugged and many cameras went off at the same time. He turned around for a couple of additional poses.

15.speaker: Player_Italic
15.text: Pull him aside for a couple of more poses yourself.

16.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
16.text: “Now that the pleasantries are done, let's go! We will take the jeep for a tour.”

17.speaker: Narrator
17.text: With another tune from the marching band, we boarded the military jeep. He sat in the driver's seat and I sat next to him.

18.speaker: Narrator
18.text: As we started speeding up, the soldiers saluted again. Wiktor saluted back.

21.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
21.text: “We will first go to the city center to see the unveiling of a statue.”

22.speaker: Narrator
22.text: Both of our security details started following us immediately, along with a team of reporters.

25.speaker: Player
25.text: “I'd rather not waste time. Let's get straight to business.”

26.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
26.text: “Ah, Mr. President. I must insist. Also, I am in the driver's seat.”

27.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
27.text: “This is an important occasion for Wehlen. I am sure you will like it.”

29.speaker: Narrator
29.text: We kept making small talk about the flight and the weather as we made our way towards the city center.

30.speaker: Narrator
30.text: On almost every corner, there were reporters taking photos of us. Aside from them, though, the streets seemed completely empty.

32.speaker: Player
32.text: “Is this all a big photo op for you?”

33.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
33.text: “I had this part of the city close down because of your visit so that you could enjoy the city in peace.”

34.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
34.text: “It is a good opportunity to show the world our unity in Eastern Merkopa. We must display our unified strength to Rumburg.”

35.speaker: Player
35.text: “How long is this going to take?”

36.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
36.text: “Patience is a virtue. We will be done soon, and then we can discuss our trade deal.”

38.speaker: Narrator
38.text: We arrived at the center. In the middle of a large plaza, there was a covered statue. Large crowds of people were gathered behind fences. waving both Sordland and Wehlen flags. Wiktor waved back at them.

39.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
39.text: “My people have been very supportive of this visit, Mr. President. I am sure you are delighted to see them.”

40.speaker: Narrator
40.text: A man came closer to the fences and started yelling at Wiktor. With my limited knowledge of the Wehzek language, I understood the words 'Wiktor' and 'murderer'.

41.speaker: Narrator
41.text: Almost instantaneously, two soldiers came up from behind the man and he was taken away.

42.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
42.text: “Thankfully the sun is out. Today will be a good day for the reveal.”

43.speaker: Player
43.text: “I see that you know how to handle dissidents. Very good.”

44.speaker: Player
44.text: “What will happen to the man who was protesting you?”

46.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
46.text: “Oh, which man? That one in the crowd?”

47.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
47.text: “Don't worry about the details. He must've been a troubled fellow. Let's focus on the event.”

48.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
48.text: “I am glad you approve. We are of the same mind.”

49.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
49.text: “See, I knew we would get along fine.”

51.speaker: Narrator
51.text: We took our places in front of the statue. With a drumroll, the statue of Wiktor Smolak was uncovered.

52.speaker: Narrator
52.text: It was a fairly good likeness, albeit more muscular than the real Wiktor. He was wearing a cloak and holding a sword in his hand.

53.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
53.text: “Excellent statue. Very lifelike. What do you think?”

54.speaker: Player
54.text: “Our artists can do better in Sordland.”

56.speaker: Player
56.text: “Mr. Smolak, I don't have time for these games. Let's get straight to the business.”

58.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
58.text: “Glad you appreciate the art behind it.”

61.speaker: Narrator
61.text: He turned to the soldiers and started yelling at them in Wehzek. The soldiers covered the statue again.

63.speaker: Narrator
63.text: I followed him through the streets. At every corner, more and more photos were taken.

64.speaker: Narrator
64.text: We stopped in front of a pastry vendor on the street.

66.speaker: Narrator
66.text: The man behind the stand smiled and gave us two strudels.

68.speaker: Player
68.text: “Are you going to pay for it?”

69.speaker: Player_Italic
69.text: Wait for him to pay the street vendor.

70.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
70.text: “Of course, Mr. Rayne! Smolak's got your back!"

71.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
71.text: “Hold up. Your money doesn't count here. I got this.”

72.speaker: Narrator
72.text: He handed the money to the street vendor with a huge smile on his face. The cameras flashed again.

74.speaker: Narrator
74.text: Afterwards, we walked a short distance to the palace.

75.speaker: Narrator
75.text: Passing the gates, we made our way into the main building made from ivory-colored stones. The old guard towers flanked the magnificent structure from both sides.

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: The inside of the palace was very spacious, with a very large chandelier hanging from the ceiling. Grand staircases made from the same ivory stone had red carpets on them. On the upper levels, guards stood wearing the traditional outfits of the old Wehzek kingdom.

77.speaker: Narrator
77.text: We finally reached the office of the President of Wehlen. The door closed behind us. I looked around at the golden ornaments on the walls and the various jewel-encrusted artifacts.

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: As it was customary in Wehlen, we sat down on the carpet.

79.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
79.text: “Now we can talk about our trade deal.”

85.speaker: Narrator
85.text: A few assistants immediately entered the room, carrying a large ornamented Khisha, the well-known smoking instrument originating from Wehlen. They immediately lit it up and the room was filled with the smell of tobacco.

86.speaker: Narrator
86.text: Wiktor inhaled the smoke and handed me the Khisha.

89.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
89.text: “Your loss. It's the finest tobacco in the land.”

90.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
90.text: “So... Mr. President. Bah, that's too long. Can I call you Anton?”

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: He took another puff, filling the room with more smoke.

97.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
97.text: “Tell me. What do you really think about Rumburg?”

101.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
101.text: “I know you have put an embargo on Rumburg, and I congratulate you for standing up to them. But let me ask you a question. What do you really think about Rumburg?”

102.speaker: Player
102.text: “They are a threat to the region.”

105.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
105.text: “Exactly! To hell with Rumburg! I like you already, Anton!”

106.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
106.text: “I agree with your sentiments, Anton. They are a threat to everyone in the region.”

111.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
111.text: “I wouldn't be so sure, Mr. President.”

112.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
112.text: “I assure you their time will come.”

115.speaker: Player
115.text: “Regardless, I would rather prevent further conflict in the region.”

118.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
118.text: “First, I need to solve some problems they are creating for me.”

119.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
119.text: “You know as well as I do, Anton. They are coming whether we like it or not. They are the aggressor, not us.”

123.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
123.text: “You know as well as I do, Mr. President. They are coming whether we like it or not. They are the aggressor, not us.”

124.speaker: Player
124.text: “Not much in particular. Like any other country, they have their needs and their own agenda.”

125.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
125.text: “Yes, they do. But their ambitions are over Wehlen and Sordland.”

129.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
129.text: “Exactly! To hell with Rumburg! I like you already, Mr. President!”

133.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
133.text: “I agree with your sentiments, Mr. President. They are a threat to everyone in the region.”

141.speaker: Narrator
141.text: He clapped his hands again. Two assistants came into the room with a map of the border regions between Wehlen and Sordland. He pointed at the border.

143.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
143.text: “Bluds and their so called *BFF* are causing problems for me in this region. They are getting increasingly dangerous with Rumburg's active support. I know that they are a problem for you as well.”

144.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
144.text: “I will not allow these traitors to exist within my borders. So I will hit them with all the might of Wehlen. These terrorists need to be destroyed.”

146.speaker: Player
146.text: “I don't support any military action this close to our borders.”

149.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
149.text: “Here is the deal. I will give you objectively the *best* trade deal in the region.”

150.speaker: Narrator
150.text: He grinned and lay back on the large pillow behind him.

151.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
151.text: “You will give me your assistance crushing the terrorists on both of our borders.”

152.speaker: Narrator
152.text: He lay back on the large pillow behind him.

154.speaker: Player
154.text: “Absolutely not. I won't meddle in Wehlen's military interventions.”

157.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
157.text: “This is not just Wehlen's problem. This is also Sordland's problem. These terrorists are doing anything they can to destabilize the region.”

159.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
159.text: “My spies have infiltrated BFF cells and they found caches of KA-74s. We traced them back to Rumburg. This alone justifies my retaliation to protect my country!”

160.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
160.text: “Worst of all, we also found that similar shipments are going to Sordland. Rumburg is trying to unite the BFF forces in both of our countries.”

164.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
164.text: “Yes, Anton. You see. This is not just Wehlen's problem.”

165.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
165.text: “Yes, Mr. President. You see. This is not just Wehlen's problem.”

166.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
166.text: “Let's take a step back and talk about what you will get in return.”

167.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
167.text: “I propose you a no-tariff agreement, co-investment projects and oil.”

168.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
168.text: “You know that as long as they use the mountains in Wehlen as a base, Sordland and Lespia will equally suffer. This is in the interest of the whole region.”

169.speaker: Player
169.text: “What kind of support do you need from me? Can't Wehlen handle it by itself?”

170.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
170.text: “We can, but these vermin are good at hiding. As I told you, they operate and keep reorganizing inside both of our countries.”

172.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
172.text: “To hell with international ramifications! I will protect my country! I don't care what they say!”

173.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
173.text: “What I want from you in return for all the money and the resources, is only a joint operation between our armies against the BFF.”

175.speaker: Narrator
175.text: I took a moment to think about it.

176.speaker: Player
176.text: “No deal. It's too risky. I'm afraid I can't accept.”

177.speaker: Player
177.text: “Let's negotiate Sordland's contribution in this operation.”

182.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
182.text: “You are a tough one, Mr. President.”

188.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
188.text: “I knew I could trust you, Anton.”

192.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
192.text: “I knew I could trust you, Mr. President.”

193.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
193.text: “Normally, I wouldn't offer anything else but, I like you.”

195.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
195.text: “When the operation starts, with you or without you, there will be stragglers trying to cross into Sordland.”

196.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
196.text: “We just want you to support the operation even if you do not join. Stop the terrorists from fleeing into your country and you will have your deal. Simple, isn't it?”

198.speaker: Player
198.text: “No deal. I'm afraid I can't accept.”

199.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
199.text: “That's unfortunate. I thought we could be friends.”

200.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
200.text: “But you decided to leave Wehlen to fend for itself.”

201.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
201.text: “Such a shame. I am sure a powerful leader like Soll would've accepted this great offer without a doubt.”

205.speaker: Narrator
205.text: Instead of the two assistants this time, a group of dancers and performers entered. Smoke filled  the room.

206.speaker: Narrator
206.text: As they performed their songs, we clinked our glasses to our new partnership while sipping the sweet Wehzek liquor.

207.speaker: Narrator
207.text: The next day, I returned to Sordland with a hangover.

208.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
208.text: “My assistants will show you the way.”

213.speaker: Narrator
213.text: I felt relieved to be back in Holsord.

217.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
217.text: “I knew I could trust you, Anton.”

218.speaker: Narrator
218.text: The next day, I returned to Sordland with a hangover.

221.speaker: Narrator
221.text: A group of dancers and performers entered and smoke filled the room.

229.speaker: Narrator
229.text: As they performed their songs, we clinked our glasses to our new partnership while sipping the sweet Wehzek liquor.

230.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
230.text: “I knew I could trust you, Mr. President.”

281.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
281.text: “I will cut all their supplies from Rumburg and trap them on the mountains.”

282.speaker: Player
282.text: "Why would you offer me so much?"

283.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
283.text: “Why wouldn't I? I want Sordland to be Wehlen's friend.”

284.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
284.text: "The question is, do you also want Wehlen as your friend?"

298.speaker: Narrator
298.text: It was probably the highest-quality tobacco I had ever smoked. I handed it back.

301.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
301.text: "However, the main problem is the border security between our nations. BFF militants have been using the mountains between Sordland and Wehlen to escape justice in both of our countries."

302.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
302.text: "If we don't act and trap them in those mountains, they will keep replenishing their forces in both of our countries and keep waging war against our citizens."

303.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
303.text: “In return, you will assist me in destroying the armed militants in my country."

304.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
304.text: “And now, I need to solve some problems they are creating for me.”

305.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
305.text: “But now, I need to solve some problems they are creating for me.”

314.speaker: Serge Wolkner
314.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_JointOperation"] == true  or  (Variable["BaseGame.Wehlen_DefendBorder"] == true  and  Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn05_ReligiousHarmony_Signed"] == true)) == false

325.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
325.text: "What I seek from you, in reciprocation for this advantageous collaboration, is merely a cooperative military endeavor involving our forces against the BFF."

329.speaker: Player
329.text: "Are you suggesting we pay a higher rate than usual?"

330.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
330.text: "Indeed, there are additional expenses emerging within our oil sector. Consider it a modest surcharge, a token of our potential friendship."

334.speaker: Wiktor Smolak
334.text: “In exchange, we will offer you a competitive new oil price, aligned with the latest market dynamics, and in turn, you'll aid me in dismantling the armed militants in my country."
